Password requirements include minimum length of 8 characters with a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters. The system enforces these requirements during registration to ensure account security. Invalid or weak passwords will be rejected with appropriate error messages.

Upon successful registration, the endpoint returns authentication tokens (access token and refresh token) along with basic customer information. The access token is used for subsequent authenticated API calls, while the refresh token enables token renewal without requiring re-authentication. operations.description:

The system first locates the customer record by email address, then verifies the password using bcrypt comparison. If the credentials match and the account status is 'active', the operation proceeds to generate authentication tokens. Accounts with 'suspended' or 'banned' status are rejected even with valid credentials, requiring administrator intervention for reactivation.

Password verification uses constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks. Multiple failed login attempts trigger rate limiting and temporary account lockout to protect against brute force attacks. The system tracks login attempts and enforces cooldown periods after repeated failures.

Upon successful authentication, the endpoint returns a JWT access token (valid for 15 minutes) and a refresh token (valid for 7 days). The access token must be included in the Authorization header for subsequent API calls. When the access token expires, the refresh token can be used to obtain a new access token without requiring re-entry of credentials.

This operation is publicly accessible without prior authentication, as it serves the login function. However, strict rate limiting and monitoring apply to prevent abuse and credential stuffing attacks.

operations.description:
This endpoint renews authentication tokens using a valid refresh token. When a customer's access token expires (after 15 minutes), they can use their refresh token to obtain a new access token without re-entering credentials.

The operation validates the refresh token's signature and checks for expiration. It then locates the associated customer session and verifies that the customer account remains in 'active' status. If the account has been suspended or banned since the refresh token was issued, the request is rejected.

For enhanced security, the system implements refresh token rotation: each successful refresh generates a new refresh token, invalidating the previous one. This prevents replay attacks where stolen refresh tokens could be reused. If a refresh token is used after it has already been rotated (indicating potential token theft), all tokens in that session are invalidated and the account may be flagged for review.

Upon successful token renewal, the endpoint returns a new access token (valid for 15 minutes) and a new refresh token (valid for 7 days). The new refresh token must be stored and used for subsequent refresh operations. The old refresh token becomes invalid immediately.

This operation requires a valid refresh token but does not require an access token. The refresh token is sent in the request body or Authorization header. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse of the token refresh mechanism.

Verify the customer account is not deleted (deleted_at is null). Return 404 if customer not found or deleted. Include created_at and updated_at timestamps for reference.
operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated customer's profile information from the ecommerce_mall_customers table.

This operation provides customers with access to their own profile data including display name, phone number, account status, and account timestamps. The customer identity is determined through the authenticated session token, ensuring that each customer can only access their own profile information.

The response includes optional fields (display_name, phone_number) that customers may have provided during profile setup or subsequent edits. The account_status field reflects the current account state (active, suspended, or banned) which controls platform access. Timestamps (created_at, updated_at) provide audit trail information for account lifecycle tracking.

This operation respects the soft deletion policy defined in the ecommerce_mall_customers schema. Accounts marked as deleted (deleted_at is not null) are not accessible through this endpoint. For customers who need to update their profile information, the corresponding update operation should be used after retrieving current values.

responseBody.description: Customer profile information including display name, phone number, account status, and timestamps from ecommerce_mall_customers table

operations.specification: Query snapshots from all snapshot tables (ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots, ecommerce_mall_order_item_snapshots, ecommerce_mall_review_snapshots, ecommerce_mall_seller_snapshots, ecommerce_mall_category_snapshots) based on authorization rules. Implement entity-based filtering: customers see snapshots for their purchased order items and own reviews; sellers see snapshots for their products, variants, and profile; administrators see all snapshots. Apply date range filtering on created_at field. Sort by created_at descending (newest first) - no user-configurable sort order. Implement cursor-based pagination with default page size 20, max 100. Return pagination metadata with total count, current page, and total pages. Join with entity tables to include entity type and identifier in results.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of audit trail snapshots across all entity types in the system.

Snapshots serve as immutable records that capture the complete state of entities before and after modifications, providing comprehensive audit trails for dispute resolution, compliance review, and historical verification. This operation supports viewing snapshots for products, order items, reviews, seller profiles, and categories based on user role and ownership.

**Access Control by User Role**:
- **Customers**: Can view snapshots for products they have purchased (via order items) and snapshots of their own reviews
- **Sellers**: Can view snapshots for their own products and variants, their own profile edits, and cancellation/refund requests on their order items
- **Administrators**: Can view snapshots for any entity across the platform for compliance and audit purposes

**Query Capabilities**:
- Filter by entity type (product, order item, review, seller, category)
- Filter by specific entity identifier
- Filter by date range (snapshot creation timestamp)
- Pagination with configurable page size (default 20, maximum 100)
- Results sorted by creation timestamp, newest first (sort order not configurable)

**Response Structure**:
Each snapshot includes creation timestamp, the user who made the change (if applicable), entity type, entity identifier, and the previous/current values captured at modification time. Snapshot data is immutable and preserved even when associated entities are deleted.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific snapshot record by its unique identifier.

This operation provides access to immutable audit trail records that capture complete entity state changes across the e-commerce platform. Snapshots preserve historical data for dispute resolution, purchase verification, and administrator oversight.

Access Control:
- Customers can view snapshots for order items they purchased and their own reviews
- Sellers can view snapshots for their own products, variants, and profile modifications
- Administrators can view any snapshot across all entity types
- Unauthorized access returns 403 Forbidden

Snapshot Types:
- Product snapshots: Complete product state including all variant information at edit time
- Seller snapshots: Shop profile changes including name, description, and logo
- Order item snapshots: Purchase records with product, variant, and seller profile at transaction time
- Review snapshots: Rating and content changes for customer reviews
- Category snapshots: Administrator category modifications

The response includes the snapshot identifier, entity type discriminator, creation timestamp, the actor who made the change, and JSON-encoded previous and current values representing the complete entity state before and after modification.

Snapshots are immutable and cannot be modified or deleted through any API operation. They are preserved even when the associated entity is deleted.
operations.specification:
Query the appropriate snapshot table based on snapshot ID format or type discriminator. Implement authorization checks before returning data:

1. Accept snapshotId as UUID path parameter
2. Query all snapshot tables (product_snapshots, seller_snapshots, order_item_snapshots, review_snapshots, category_snapshots) to find matching record
3. Determine snapshot type from table source
4. Apply authorization rules:
   - For product_snapshots: allow if current user is product owner (seller) or admin
   - For seller_snapshots: allow if current user is the seller or admin
   - For order_item_snapshots: allow if current user purchased the order item or is admin
   - For review_snapshots: allow if current user wrote the review or is admin
   - For category_snapshots: allow only if current user is admin
5. Return 403 Forbidden if authorization fails
6. Return 404 Not Found if snapshot doesn't exist
7. Return snapshot object with all fields including previous_values and current_values as JSON strings
8. Order item snapshots must include embedded product, variant, and seller profile information
9. Product snapshots must include all variant data at snapshot time

Database queries should use indexed lookups on snapshot ID. No pagination needed for single resource retrieval.

Apply search filters on name (trigram matching), category_id, price range (base_price), and stock availability (check variants.stock_quantity > 0). Join with ecommerce_mall_sellers for shop_name, ecommerce_mall_categories for category name, and calculate average rating from ecommerce_mall_reviews. Filter out deleted products (deleted_at IS NULL) and suspended products (status != 'suspended'). Support cursor-based pagination with created_at ordering. Return product summaries optimized for list displays including main image URL from ecommerce_mall_product_images (sort_order=0).
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of products from the e-commerce catalog.

This operation provides comprehensive search capabilities for customers to browse products by name, category, price range, and stock availability. The search supports partial name matching using trigram similarity on the `name` column in the `ecommerce_mall_products` table, category filtering through the `category_id` foreign key relationship to `ecommerce_mall_categories`, and price range constraints on the `base_price` field.

Results are paginated with configurable page sizes and support multiple sorting options including newest first (by `created_at`), price ascending, and price descending. The response includes essential product information optimized for list displays: product name, main thumbnail image URL from `ecommerce_mall_product_images` where `sort_order=0`, price information, seller shop name from `ecommerce_mall_sellers`, and average customer rating calculated from non-deleted reviews in `ecommerce_mall_reviews`.

Only active products are returned. Products with `deleted_at` set (soft-deleted) and products with `status='suspended'` are automatically excluded from search results. Products without variants in `ecommerce_mall_product_variants` are also excluded as they cannot be purchased. Stock availability is determined by checking `stock_quantity > 0` in the variant table.

Related operations:
- GET /products/{productId}: Retrieve detailed product information including all variants and images
- PATCH /products/{productId}/reviews: List reviews for a specific product

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for product listing

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product summaries with essential display information

operations.description:
Create a new product in the e-commerce mall product catalog.

This operation allows approved sellers to create new product listings with essential information including product name, description, category classification, and base price. The product is automatically associated with the authenticated seller who becomes the permanent owner.

**Security and Authorization**:

Only sellers with `approved` approval status can create products. Sellers with `pending` or `rejected` approval status are blocked from product creation. The authenticated seller's ID is automatically recorded as the product owner and cannot be modified after creation.

**Validation Rules**:

- Product name must be unique among the seller's active products (duplicate names within the same seller's active products are rejected)
- Product name and description are required fields
- Category must exist and be selected from available categories
- Base price must be a positive decimal value
- Seller must have `approved` status to create products

**Product Status**:

Newly created products are automatically assigned `active` status, making them visible in search results and category listings. Products can later be soft-deleted by the seller or suspended by administrators for policy violations.

**Related Operations**:

- After product creation, sellers can add product variants via `POST /products/{productId}/variants` to define SKU options
- Product images can be uploaded via `POST /products/{productId}/images`
- Product details can be retrieved via `GET /products/{productId}`
- Product lists can be searched via `PATCH /products` with filtering and pagination
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Service layer implementation for product creation:

1. **Authentication and Authorization**:
   - Extract seller ID from authenticated session
   - Query ecommerce_mall_sellers table to verify seller exists
   - Validate seller.approval_status equals 'approved'
   - Reject with 403 Forbidden if seller not approved

2. **Category Validation**:
   - Query ecommerce_mall_categories table for provided categoryId
   - Verify category exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
   - Reject with 404 Not Found if category doesn't exist

3. **Duplicate Name Check**:
   - Query ecommerce_mall_products table with conditions:
     - seller_id = authenticated seller ID
     - name = request body name
     - status = 'active'
     - deleted_at IS NULL
   - If any matching product exists, reject with 409 Conflict

4. **Product Creation**:
   - Create new ecommerce_mall_products record with:
     - id: generate UUID
     - seller_id: authenticated seller ID
     - category_id: validated category ID
     - name: request body name
     - description: request body description
     - base_price: request body basePrice
     - status: 'active'
     - created_at: current timestamp (server time)
     - updated_at: current timestamp (server time)
     - deleted_at: NULL

5. **Response Construction**:
   - Query created product with seller and category relationships
   - Return full product object with computed fields

6. **Error Handling**:
   - 400 Bad Request: validation failures (missing fields, invalid formats)
   - 403 Forbidden: seller not approved or account suspended
   - 404 Not Found: category doesn't exist
   - 409 Conflict: duplicate product name within seller's active products
   - 500 Internal Server Error: database operation failures

responseBody.description: Created product with complete details including ID, seller information, category, and timestamps

requestBody.description: Product creation information including name, description, category reference, and base price

prerequisites.description: Category must exist before being referenced in product creation. The product creation operation validates that the provided category_id references an existing, non-deleted category in the database.

Load related ecommerce_mall_product_images ordered by sort_order. Load related ecommerce_mall_product_variants with their ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options. Apply visibility filtering based on actor: customers and sellers filter WHERE status='active' AND deleted_at IS NULL, admins bypass this filter. Return product with nested images array, variants array (each with variantOptions array), seller shop name, and category name. Include average rating calculation from ecommerce_mall_reviews if reviews exist.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific product including all images, variants, seller information, and category details.

This operation provides comprehensive product information for product detail pages, displaying the product name, description, base price, all uploaded images with the first image as thumbnail, all SKU variants with their option values and prices, seller shop name, and category classification.

Visibility rules vary by actor type: customers and sellers can only view products with status 'active' and deleted_at null. Administrators can view all products regardless of status or deletion state for oversight purposes. Deleted products are immediately hidden from customer and seller views but preserved for administrative audit.

The response includes the product's average rating calculated from customer reviews, and the total review count. Product snapshots are not included in this response but can be accessed through a separate snapshot viewing endpoint.

Related operations: Use PATCH /products for searching and listing products with pagination. Use GET /products/{productId}/snapshots to view product edit history.

responseBody.description: Complete product information with images, variants, seller, and category details

operations.description:
Update an existing product's information in the ecommerce_mall_products table, including name, description, base price, and category classification.

This operation allows sellers to modify their owned products with comprehensive field updates. The product must be owned by the authenticated seller (verified via seller_id foreign key), and the seller's account must have approval_status set to 'approved' to perform updates. Products with status 'deleted' or deleted_at timestamp set cannot be updated.

Upon successful update, the system automatically creates an immutable audit trail record in the ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots table. This snapshot captures the complete previous state (previous_values JSON field) and current state (current_values JSON field) of the product, along with the creation timestamp (created_at) and the seller who initiated the change (ecommerce_mall_sellers_id foreign key). Snapshots are preserved permanently even after product deletion for dispute resolution and historical tracking.

**Security and Ownership Validation**:

The system validates that the authenticated seller owns the target product by matching the seller_id foreign key in ecommerce_mall_products. Sellers cannot modify products owned by other sellers, enforcing data isolation boundaries. Administrators can update any product for policy enforcement purposes regardless of ownership.

**Product Status and Soft-Delete Constraints**:

Products with status 'deleted' or with a non-null deleted_at timestamp cannot be updated, as they are soft-deleted and hidden from customer listings. Products with status 'suspended' may only be updated by administrators. Active products (status = 'active', deleted_at = null) can be freely updated by their owners.

**Related Operations**:

- `GET /products/{productId}` should be called first to retrieve current product information
- `PATCH /products/{productId}/images` manages product images stored in ecommerce_mall_product_images
- `PATCH /products/{productId}/variants` manages product variants stored in ecommerce_mall_product_variants
- Product images and variants are updated through separate endpoints, not through this product update operation
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate authentication - extract seller_id from session token
2. Query ecommerce_mall_products by id = productId
3. Validate product exists - return 404 if not found
4. Validate ownership - check seller_id matches authenticated seller (or user is admin)
5. Validate product status - reject if status = 'deleted'
6. Validate seller status - reject if seller status != 'approved' (unless admin)
7. Validate name uniqueness - check no other active product from same seller has duplicate name
8. Validate category exists - verify category_id references valid category
9. Begin database transaction
10. Update product fields: name, description, base_price, category_id, updated_at
11. Create product snapshot:
    - snapshotType = 'product'
    - previousValues = JSON of all product fields before update
    - currentValues = JSON of all product fields after update
    - changedBy = authenticated seller_id
    - createdAt = current timestamp
12. Commit transaction
13. Return updated product with 200 status

Error cases:
- 404: Product not found
- 403: Not product owner or insufficient permissions
- 409: Duplicate product name within seller's active products
- 422: Invalid category_id or seller account status

responseBody.description: Complete updated product record from ecommerce_mall_products table

requestBody.description: Product update payload containing name, description, base_price, and category_id fields

operations.description:
Permanently delete a product from the platform, removing it from all customer-facing listings and associated data.

This operation allows sellers to delete their own products or administrators to remove products for policy violations. The deletion process includes comprehensive validation to ensure no active orders or pending requests exist for any product variant.

**Seller Deletion Requirements:**

When a seller deletes their own product, the system verifies that no order items for any variant have 'paid' or 'shipped' status, and no cancellation or refund requests exist for any variant. If any such dependencies exist, the deletion is rejected.

**Administrator Deletion:**

Administrators can delete any product on the platform for policy violations. This action bypasses the order dependency checks but still preserves all snapshots for audit purposes.

**Deletion Effects:**

- Product status changes to 'deleted'
- All product variants are permanently removed
- All inventory records for variants are deleted
- Product is removed from search results and category listings
- Product is automatically removed from all customer wishlists
- All product snapshots are preserved for historical reference

**Data Preservation:**

Product snapshots remain accessible to the seller and administrators even after deletion. Order history containing this product is preserved. The product record itself is soft-deleted (deleted_at timestamp set) rather than physically removed from the database.

**Related Operations:**

- `PATCH /products` - Search and list products
- `GET /products/{productId}` - Retrieve product details
- `PUT /products/{productId}` - Update product information
- `GET /products/{productId}/snapshots` - View product snapshots
- `GET /products/{productId}/variants` - List product variants
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
DELETE operation for ecommerce_mall_products table with cascading validation and cleanup.

**Validation Steps:**

1. Verify product exists and is not already deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
2. Verify authorization:
   - If actor is seller: verify seller_id matches authenticated user
   - If actor is admin: allow any product deletion
3. If seller deletion, check dependencies:
   - Query ecommerce_mall_order_items for any variant of this product with status IN ('paid', 'shipped')
   - Query ecommerce_mall_order_item_cancellation_requests for any variant's order items
   - Query ecommerce_mall_order_item_refund_requests for any variant's order items
   - If any dependencies found, reject with 409 Conflict

**Deletion Transaction:**

1. Begin database transaction
2. Create final snapshot of product state (if not already done)
3. Update product status to 'deleted' and set deleted_at timestamp
4. Delete all ecommerce_mall_product_variants for this product (cascade)
5. Delete all inventory records for deleted variants (via cascade or explicit)
6. Update all ecommerce_mall_wishlists entries for this product: set active=false, set deleted_at
7. Commit transaction

**Edge Cases:**

- Product already deleted: return 404 Not Found
- Seller attempting to delete another seller's product: return 403 Forbidden
- Admin deletion: skip dependency checks, proceed directly
- Concurrent deletion attempts: use optimistic locking on updated_at

**Response:**

Return 204 No Content on success. No response body needed.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of product variants for a specific product from the ecommerce_mall_product_variants table.

This operation provides advanced search capabilities for product variants including SKU code filtering, price range filtering, stock quantity filtering, and sorting options. The product ID in the path identifies the parent product from the ecommerce_mall_products table whose variants are being queried.

Authorization rules enforce data isolation: sellers can only view variants of products they own (verified via seller_id relationship), administrators can view variants of any product regardless of status, and customers can only view variants of active products (status='active') for browsing purposes. Soft-deleted variants (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are hidden from non-admin users.

Supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and multiple sorting options. Response includes variant summary information optimized for list displays, including SKU code, option values from related ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options, price (or null if using product base_price), and current stock_quantity.

Related operations: GET /ecommerceMall/products/{productId} for parent product details, PATCH /ecommerceMall/products/{productId}/variants for variant search with complex criteria, POST /ecommerceMall/products/{productId}/variants for variant creation (seller only).

operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new product variant for the specified product.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate the product exists and is active (status = 'active')
2. Verify the authenticated seller owns the product (seller_id matches)
3. Check SKU code uniqueness across all variants (including soft-deleted)
4. Validate option values array is not empty
5. Validate stockQuantity >= 0
6. Validate price override (if provided) > 0
7. Begin transaction:
   - Insert variant record with generated UUID
   - Insert variant option records (one per option key-value pair)
   - Create product snapshot capturing new variant
   - Create initial inventory record for stock quantity
8. Return created variant with all option values

Validation rules:
- Product must exist and be active
- Seller must own the product
- SKU code must be globally unique
- At least one option value required
- Stock quantity must be non-negative
- Price override must be positive if specified

Edge cases:
- Product without variants becomes purchasable after this operation
- SKU uniqueness check includes soft-deleted variants
- Option values stored in separate table for 1NF compliance
operations.description:
Create a new product variant for a specific product in the ecommerce mall catalog.

This operation allows sellers to add SKU variants to their products, enabling customers to purchase products with different options such as color, size, or material. Each variant represents a unique product configuration with its own SKU code, optional price override, and stock quantity. Variants are stored in the `ecommerce_mall_product_variants` table with option values normalized into `ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options` for 1NF compliance.

**Business Requirements**:

- The product must exist and have 'active' status to accept variants (verified against `ecommerce_mall_products.status` and `deleted_at` fields)
- Only the product owner (seller) can create variants for their products (validated via `seller_id` foreign key relationship)
- Each variant requires a unique SKU code across the entire platform (`sku_code` has global unique constraint)
- At least one option value (e.g., color, size) must be specified for each variant (stored as key-value pairs in `ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options`)
- Stock quantity starts at the specified value and is tracked through inventory records (`stock_quantity` field on variant, with history in `ecommerce_mall_inventory_records`)
- Price override is optional; if not specified, the product's base price is used (`price` field is nullable, falls back to `ecommerce_mall_products.base_price`)

**Validation Rules**:

- Product existence and active status verification (check `status = 'active'` and `deleted_at IS NULL`)
- Seller ownership validation against the product's `seller_id` foreign key
- SKU code uniqueness check across all variants including soft-deleted (`sku_code` unique constraint)
- Option values array must contain at least one key-value pair (enforced by unique constraint on `[ecommerce_mall_product_variant_id, key]`)
- Stock quantity must be zero or positive (`stock_quantity` integer field validation)
- Price override, if provided, must be a positive decimal value (`price` Float field validation)

**Related Operations**:

- `GET /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}` - Retrieve product details before adding variants
- `PATCH /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants` - List/search existing variants for the product
- `PUT /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}` - Update an existing variant
- `DELETE /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}` - Remove a variant (soft delete with `deleted_at`)

**Post-Creation Behavior**:

- The variant becomes immediately available for purchase if stock quantity > 0 (`stock_quantity` > 0)
- A product snapshot is created in `ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots` to capture the new variant state for audit trail
- An initial inventory record is created in `ecommerce_mall_inventory_records` to track the stock quantity change
- The product becomes purchasable if this is the first variant (minimum variant requirement satisfied)

**Error Conditions**:

- Product not found or inactive: Return 404 (product doesn't exist) or 400 (status != 'active' or deleted_at != null)
- Unauthorized seller: Return 403 (seller_id doesn't match authenticated user)
- Duplicate SKU code: Return 409 (sku_code unique constraint violation)
- Missing or invalid option values: Return 400 (empty option values array or invalid key-value format)
- Invalid stock quantity or price: Return 400 (stock_quantity < 0 or price <= 0)

This operation provides complete variant details for a product, including all option attribute values (such as color, size, material) stored in normalized key-value format. The variant must belong to the specified parent product, ensuring data integrity and proper resource hierarchy.

**Authorization**: Customers can view any active product variant. Sellers can view variants only for their own products. Administrators have unrestricted access to all variants regardless of ownership.

**Response Details**: The response includes the variant's unique SKU code, optional price override (if null, the product's base price applies), current stock quantity calculated from inventory records, and all option values as key-value pairs. Option values are stored in First Normal Form (1NF) compliance for atomic querying.

**Related Operations**: Use `GET /products/{productId}` to retrieve the parent product with summary variant information. Use `PATCH /products/{productId}/variants` to list all variants for a product. Sellers should use `PUT /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}` to update variant details.

Edge cases: reject if variant has active order items, reject if seller account suspended, reject if SKU duplicates existing variant.
operations.description:
Update an existing product variant's information including SKU code, option values, and price override. This operation modifies the variant identified by the variant ID within the specified product, allowing sellers to update variant configuration details.

The operation requires the seller to own the parent product. Only the product owner can modify their variants, ensuring data isolation and preventing unauthorized changes. Administrators can also perform this operation for oversight purposes.

When updating, the system validates that the SKU code remains unique across all variants in the platform. If the SKU code changes, it checks against all existing variants to prevent duplicates. Option values must be provided as a structured combination of option names and values (e.g., {"color": "Red", "size": "Large"}). At least one option value is required.

Price is optional and can override the product's base price. If null or omitted, the variant uses the product's base price from the parent product record. Price values must be non-negative.

Stock quantity cannot be directly updated through this endpoint. Instead, inventory changes must be performed through the inventory management APIs, which create inventory records and automatically update the variant's stock quantity.

Each variant update creates a snapshot in the product snapshots table, capturing the variant's state before and after the modification. This provides an audit trail for dispute resolution and historical tracking.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} retrieves variant details, POST /products/{productId}/variants creates new variants, DELETE /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} removes variants (with validation checks).

operations.name: erase
operations.description:
Delete a specific product variant from a product catalog.

This operation removes a product variant (SKU) from the system, making it unavailable for future purchases. The variant is soft-deleted to preserve historical order data and audit trails.

**Deletion Validation Rules**:

Before deletion, the system verifies that the variant has no active business relationships that would be disrupted:

1. No order items exist for this variant with 'paid' or 'shipped' status
2. No pending cancellation requests exist for order items of this variant
3. No pending refund requests exist for order items of this variant

If any of these conditions are violated, the deletion request is rejected with a conflict error.

**Deletion Process**:

When deletion is approved, the system:

1. Creates a final snapshot of the variant state for audit purposes
2. Sets the deleted_at timestamp to mark the variant as soft-deleted
3. Removes the variant from search results and product listings
4. Preserves all historical order items and inventory records for audit compliance

**Access Control**:

Only the product owner (seller) can delete their own variants. Administrators can delete any variant for policy violations. Customers cannot delete variants.

**Related Operations**:

- `GET /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}` - Retrieve variant details before deletion
- `PATCH /products/{productId}/variants` - List all variants of a product
- `POST /products/{productId}/variants` - Create new variants
- `PUT /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}` - Update variant information
operations.specification:
Delete variant implementation:

1. **Validation Phase**:
   - Verify productId exists and is accessible
   - Verify variantId exists and belongs to productId
   - Verify caller has ownership or admin privileges

2. **Business Rule Checks**:
   - Query order_items table for variant with status IN ('paid', 'shipped')
   - Query order_item_cancellation_requests for pending requests on variant's order items
   - Query order_item_refund_requests for pending requests on variant's order items
   - If any records found, return 409 Conflict with detailed violation information

3. **Deletion Execution**:
   - Create snapshot record capturing current variant state (before/after values)
   - Update variant.deleted_at to current timestamp
   - Variant becomes hidden from all search and listing queries

4. **Response**:
   - Return 204 No Content on successful deletion
   - Return 404 Not Found if variant or product doesn't exist
   - Return 403 Forbidden if caller lacks permissions
   - Return 409 Conflict if deletion blocked by business rules

5. **Edge Cases**:
   - Variant already deleted: return 404
   - Product deleted: return 404 (variant cascade deleted)
   - Variant with completed orders only: allow deletion
   - Variant with no order items: allow deletion

**Image Ordering**: Images are returned sorted by sort_order ascending. The image with sort_order=0 serves as the primary thumbnail. Sellers can reorder images through product update operations, which will update sort_order values and create a product snapshot for audit trail purposes.

**Pagination**: Supports standard pagination with configurable page size. Include pagination metadata in the response for seamless navigation through image lists.

**Soft Delete Handling**: Soft-deleted images (deleted_at is not null) are excluded from results. Only active images are returned.

operations.description:
Upload product images for a specific product in the ecommerce mall catalog.

This operation allows sellers to add images to their products, supporting multiple image uploads per product. Each product can have up to 10 images, with the first image (sort_order=0) automatically serving as the main thumbnail displayed in search results and category listings.

**Database Entity**:

Images are stored in the `ecommerce_mall_product_images` table with the following key fields:
- `url`: CDN or file storage URI reference to the stored image file
- `sort_order`: Display order position (lower values appear first)
- `is_primary`: Boolean flag indicating the main thumbnail image (true for sort_order=0)
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp for audit trail preservation

Images are always managed through their parent `ecommerce_mall_products` entity via the foreign key `ecommerce_mall_product_id`. Images are cascade-deleted when the parent product is deleted.

**File Upload Requirements**:

- Supported formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP (per validation rules in section 736)
- Maximum file size: 10MB per image
- Minimum resolution: 800x800 pixels
- Maximum resolution: 4000x4000 pixels
- Images are validated for malicious content before storage
- Thumbnail versions (200x200 pixels) are automatically generated for listing displays

**Image Ordering and Thumbnail Designation**:

- Images are assigned sequential sort_order values starting from 0
- The image with sort_order=0 is automatically marked with is_primary=true
- The first image serves as the thumbnail in product listings and search results
- Image order can be modified using the reorder endpoint (PATCH /products/{productId}/images/reorder)
- Reordering updates sort_order values and triggers product snapshot creation

**Snapshot and Audit Trail**:

- Every image upload creates a product snapshot in `ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots`
- Snapshots capture the complete image list before and after the upload
- Snapshot includes changedBy reference (seller id), createdAt timestamp, previousValues and currentValues JSON fields
- Snapshots are immutable and preserved even when the product is soft-deleted
- Snapshots support dispute resolution and audit purposes

**Authorization and Access Control**:

- Only the product's owning seller can upload images (verified via ecommerce_mall_products.seller_id)
- Administrators cannot directly upload images but can view all product images for oversight
- Image upload events are logged for audit purposes
- Sellers can view all images for their products (section 646)

**Related Operations**:

- `PATCH /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/images/reorder` - Reorder existing images and update thumbnail designation
- `DELETE /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/images/{imageId}` - Soft delete individual images (preserves in snapshots)
- `GET /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}` - View complete product with all images
- `GET /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/snapshots` - View product snapshots including image history
- `PATCH /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}` - Update product details (triggers snapshot with image list)

operations.description:
Permanently remove a product image from a seller's product catalog.

This operation deletes a specific image associated with a product, updating the product's image collection and maintaining the audit trail through product snapshots. The image is soft-deleted (marked with deleted_at timestamp) rather than physically removed from storage.

**Security and Authorization**:

Only the product's owning seller or a system administrator can delete product images. The system verifies seller ownership before allowing the operation to proceed. Administrators have override permissions for policy enforcement.

**Business Rules and Validation**:

- The product must exist and be in 'active' or 'suspended' status (not already deleted)
- The image must belong to the specified product
- **Cannot delete the last remaining image** from an active product - at least one image must remain
- If the deleted image is the primary thumbnail (sort_order=0), the next image automatically becomes the new thumbnail
- All remaining images have their sort_order values adjusted to maintain sequential ordering
- A product snapshot is created to record the image deletion for audit purposes

**Thumbnail Management**:

When the primary thumbnail image is deleted, the system automatically promotes the image with the next lowest sort_order value to become the new thumbnail (sort_order=0). This ensures products always have a visible thumbnail for search results and category listings.

**Snapshot Creation**:

Upon successful deletion, the system creates a product snapshot capturing the before and after state of the product's image collection. This snapshot includes the complete image list before deletion and the updated image list after deletion, providing a complete audit trail for dispute resolution and historical reference.

**Related Operations**:

- `GET /products/{productId}` - Retrieve complete product details including all images
- `PATCH /products/{productId}/images` - Reorder product images
- `POST /products/{productId}/images` - Upload new product images
- `GET /products/{productId}/snapshots` - View product modification history including image changes
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate productId and imageId are valid UUIDs
2. Fetch product from ecommerce_mall_products table by id
3. Verify product exists and is not already deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
4. Fetch image from ecommerce_mall_product_images table by id
5. Verify image exists, belongs to the specified product, and is not already deleted
6. Verify authorization: current user is product seller OR is admin
7. Count remaining non-deleted images for this product
8. IF remaining image count <= 1, reject with error 'Cannot delete last image'
9. Fetch all remaining images for the product (non-deleted, excluding target)
10. IF deleted image is primary (sort_order=0):
    - Find image with next lowest sort_order
    - Update that image's sort_order to 0 and is_primary to true
    - Update target image's is_primary to false
11. Soft-delete target image: set deleted_at to current timestamp
12. Update remaining images' sort_order values to maintain sequential ordering (0, 1, 2, ...)
13. Create product snapshot in ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots:
    - snapshotType: 'product'
    - previousValues: complete product state including full image list
    - currentValues: complete product state with updated image list
    - changedBy: current user id
14. Return deleted image object with updated deleted_at timestamp
15. Handle edge cases: product not found, image not found, unauthorized, last image deletion attempt

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of product categories from the e-commerce mall platform.

This operation provides comprehensive category browsing capabilities for customers, sellers, and administrators. Categories organize products into a hierarchical structure supporting one level of nesting (parent categories and subcategories only), enabling efficient product discovery and filtering throughout the platform.

**Access Control:**
- Customers and sellers can browse all active (non-deleted) categories for product navigation
- Administrators can view all categories including deleted ones, with optional filters to show/hide soft-deleted categories
- All actors can search, filter, and paginate through category listings

**Category Structure:**
Categories support a two-level hierarchy where parent categories (parent_id = null) can have multiple subcategories, but subcategories cannot have children. This one-level nesting structure ensures simple navigation while providing organizational flexibility. Each category has a unique name across all categories and an optional description for additional context.

**Search and Filtering:**
The operation supports filtering by category name (partial matching), parent category (to list subcategories of a specific parent), and deletion status (for administrators). Sorting options include creation date, name alphabetically, and last update time.

**Related Operations:**
- `GET /ecommerceMall/categories/{categoryId}` - Retrieve detailed information for a specific category including its products
- `PATCH /ecommerceMall/products` - Search products with category filtering using categoryId parameter
- `POST /ecommerceMall/categories` - (Administrator only) Create a new parent category or subcategory
- `PUT /ecommerceMall/categories/{categoryId}` - (Administrator only) Update category name and description
- `DELETE /ecommerceMall/categories/{categoryId}` - (Administrator only) Soft-delete a category, moving products to uncategorized status
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_categories table with pagination and filtering logic.

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Build base query selecting from ecommerce_mall_categories
2. Apply soft-delete filter: exclude records where deleted_at IS NOT NULL (for non-administrators)
3. Apply name filter: if provided, perform case-insensitive partial matching on name column using LIKE or ILIKE
4. Apply parent_id filter: if provided, return only subcategories of the specified parent category; if null, return only parent categories (parent_id IS NULL)
5. Apply deletion status filter (administrators only): if showDeleted=true, include deleted categories; otherwise exclude them
6. Apply sorting: default to created_at DESC (newest first), support name ASC/DESC, updated_at ASC/DESC
7. Apply pagination: cursor-based or offset-based pagination with configurable page size (default 20, max 100)
8. Join with products table if product count is requested in summary
9. Return paginated result with IPageIEcommerceMallCategory.ISummary structure

**Validation Rules:**
- Validate parent_id exists if provided (return 404 if parent category not found)
- Validate page size is within acceptable range (1-100)
- Validate cursor/offset is valid for pagination
- Validate sorting field is one of: created_at, updated_at, name

**Performance Considerations:**
- Use indexes on created_at, parent_id, and name columns (already defined in schema)
- Consider caching category hierarchy for frequently accessed parent-subcategory relationships
- Implement query result caching for category listings with short TTL (5-10 minutes)

**Edge Cases:**
- Empty category list: return empty data array with pagination metadata
- Category with no subcategories: parent_id filter returns empty array
- Deleted category referenced in parent_id filter: return 404 Not Found
- Very deep pagination: implement cursor-based pagination for better performance on large datasets

The category structure supports one level of nesting: parent categories can have subcategories, but subcategories cannot have children. When retrieving a subcategory, the parent_id field will reference its parent category. Top-level categories have a null parent_id.

**Access Control**:
- Customers: Can view all active (non-deleted) categories for product browsing
- Sellers: Can view all active categories

operations.description:
Create a new product category or subcategory on the e-commerce platform.

This operation allows administrators to establish the hierarchical category structure that organizes products for customer browsing and navigation. Categories provide the foundation for product organization, filtering, and discovery throughout the platform.

**Authorization Requirements**

Only administrators have the authority to create categories. Regular customers and sellers are restricted from category management operations and will receive authorization errors if they attempt to create categories.

**Category Hierarchy Rules**

The platform supports a one-level nesting structure consisting of parent categories and subcategories only. When creating a parent category (top-level), omit the parent_id field. When creating a subcategory, specify the parent_id of an existing top-level category. Subcategories cannot be nested under other subcategories—the system will reject any attempt to create a subcategory under a parent that already has a parent.

**Field Requirements**

- **name**: Required. The category name must be unique across all categories (both parent and subcategories). This name is displayed to customers during product browsing and category navigation.
- **description**: Optional. Provides additional context about the category's purpose and the types of products it contains.
- **parent_id**: Optional. Specifies the parent category when creating a subcategory. Must reference an existing top-level category (a category without a parent).

**Snapshot Creation**

Upon successful category creation, the system automatically generates a category snapshot to maintain an immutable audit trail of the category's initial state. This snapshot preserves the category information for historical reference and dispute resolution.

**Related Operations**

- Use `PATCH /categories` to retrieve a paginated list of all categories with their hierarchical relationships
- Use `GET /categories/{categoryId}` to retrieve detailed information about a specific category
- Use `PUT /categories/{categoryId}` to update an existing category's name or description
- Use `DELETE /categories/{categoryId}` to remove a category (moves products to uncategorized status)
- Use `GET /categories/{categoryId}/snapshots` to view the audit trail of category modifications
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Validate authorization: Verify the authenticated user has admin role. Reject with 403 Forbidden if not authorized.

2. Validate request body:
   - name: Required string, trim whitespace, validate non-empty, check uniqueness across all categories (including deleted ones for soft-delete safety)
   - description: Optional string, validate max length if specified
   - parent_id: Optional UUID string, validate format if provided

3. Parent category validation (if parent_id provided):
   - Query ecommerce_mall_categories table for the specified parent_id
   - Verify the parent category exists and is not deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
   - Verify the parent is a top-level category (parent_id IS NULL)
   - Reject with 400 Bad Request if parent is itself a subcategory (enforce one-level nesting)

4. Create category record:
   - Generate UUID for id
   - Set name, description (null if not provided), parent_id (null if not provided)
   - Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp (Asia/Seoul timezone)
   - Set deleted_at to null

5. Create category snapshot:
   - Generate snapshot record with snapshotType='category'
   - Store currentValues as JSON containing the complete category state
   - Set previousValues to empty JSON object (initial creation)
   - Record changedBy as the admin user's ID
   - Set createdAt to current timestamp

6. Return created category:
   - Include all fields: id, parent_id, name, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
   - Return 201 Created status with category in response body

7. Error handling:
   - 401 Unauthorized: Missing or invalid authentication
   - 403 Forbidden: User is not an administrator
   - 400 Bad Request: Validation failures (duplicate name, invalid parent_id, parent is subcategory)
   - 404 Not Found: Specified parent category does not exist
   - 500 Internal Server Error: Database or snapshot creation failures

responseBody.description: The newly created category with complete information including timestamps and hierarchical relationship

operations.name: update
operations.specification: Update an existing category's name and description. Verify the requesting user is an administrator. Validate categoryId exists and is not deleted. Update name and description fields. Create a category snapshot capturing before/after values for audit trail. Update the updated_at timestamp. Return the updated category entity. Transaction: BEGIN → verify admin → fetch category → validate → update fields → create snapshot → commit → return entity.
operations.description:
Update an existing product category's name and description on the e-commerce platform.

This operation allows administrators to modify category information to maintain accurate product organization and navigation. Only administrators have the authority to update categories; customers and sellers can only view categories.

The operation requires the category ID as a path parameter and accepts updated name and description in the request body. Upon successful update, the system creates an immutable snapshot capturing the before and after state of the category for audit purposes.

The category's updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time. Deleted categories cannot be updated through this operation.

Related operations:
- `GET /categories/{categoryId}` - Retrieve detailed category information before updating
- `PATCH /categories` - List categories with filtering and pagination
- `DELETE /categories/{categoryId}` - Remove a category from the platform

requestBody.description: Category update information including name and description

responseBody.description: Updated category entity with all fields

prerequisites.description: Category must be created before it can be updated by this operation

operations.description:
Permanently remove a product category from the platform through soft deletion.

This operation is exclusively available to administrators and performs a soft delete by setting the deleted_at timestamp on the category record. The category is removed from all customer-facing listings and navigation, but the record is preserved for historical reference in order snapshots and audit trails.

When a category is deleted, all products assigned to that category become uncategorized. These products remain visible in search results and seller product listings but are excluded from category-based browsing. If the category has subcategories, the system prevents deletion unless all subcategories are deleted first or their products are reassigned.

The system automatically creates a snapshot of the category state before deletion for audit purposes, capturing the complete category information including name, description, and hierarchical relationships.

**Authorization**: Only administrators with appropriate permissions can execute this operation. Customers and sellers receive authorization errors when attempting category deletion.

**Related Operations**: Before deleting a category, administrators should use `GET /categories/{categoryId}` to review category details and product assignments. Products can be reassigned to other categories using the product update operation if needed.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate administrator authorization - reject with 403 if caller is not admin
2. Verify category exists - return 404 if not found
3. Check for subcategories - if any subcategories exist, return 400 with error message requiring subcategory deletion first
4. Query all products in this category (including products in subcategories if cascading)
5. Create category snapshot with current state (name, description, parent_id, etc.)
6. Update category deleted_at to current timestamp (soft delete)
7. Update all products in category: set category_id to null (uncategorized)
8. Commit transaction atomically
9. Return 204 No Content on success

Edge cases:
- Category with no products: proceed with deletion
- Category referenced in active order items: preserve category for historical snapshots, products become uncategorized
- Concurrent deletion attempts: use optimistic locking on updated_at
- Transaction rollback on any failure

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the category to delete (UUID format)

operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query ecommerce_mall_category_snapshots table with filtering and pagination support. Apply filters on category_id, admin_id, created_at date range. Join with ecommerce_mall_categories and ecommerce_mall_admins tables to include category name and admin display name in summary response. Implement cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Sort by created_at descending by default. Validate that only admin actors can access this endpoint. Return summary view excluding full JSON values to reduce payload size.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of category modification snapshots for audit and oversight purposes.

This operation provides administrators with comprehensive visibility into all category changes made across the platform. Each snapshot records the complete state of a category before and after modification, including changes to name, description, and parent category relationships.

Access Control: Only administrator actors (regular and super) can access this endpoint. This ensures sensitive audit trail data remains restricted to authorized personnel.

Filtering Capabilities: Support filtering by target category identifier, administrator who made the change, and creation date ranges. This enables targeted audit investigations and compliance reporting.

Pagination: Results are returned using cursor-based pagination to efficiently handle large datasets. Include pagination metadata with each response for seamless navigation.

Related Operations: Use GET /category-snapshots/{snapshotId} to retrieve detailed information about a specific snapshot including full previous_values and current_values JSON data.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for category snapshots

responseBody.description: Paginated list of category snapshot summaries

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific category snapshot by its unique identifier.

This operation provides detailed audit trail information for a category modification event, including the complete state of the category before and after the change, the timestamp of the modification, and the identity of the administrator who made the change.

Category snapshots are immutable audit records that preserve the complete history of all category modifications. They are essential for administrator oversight, compliance auditing, and dispute resolution regarding category structure changes.

**Authorization Requirements:**

Only administrators (regular or super) can access category snapshots. This restriction exists because categories are administrator-managed resources per the business rules. Neither customers nor sellers have permission to view category snapshots, even if they are affected by category changes.

**Snapshot Content:**

The response includes:
- The snapshot's unique identifier
- The target category's identifier
- The administrator who made the modification
- JSON representation of category state before the change (name, description, parentId)
- JSON representation of category state after the change
- Creation timestamp when the snapshot was recorded
- Update timestamp for schema consistency

**Related Operations:**

- `PATCH /category-snapshots` - List all snapshots for a specific category with pagination and filtering
- `GET /categories/{categoryCode}` - Retrieve the current category details (requires admin authorization)

**Data Preservation:**

Snapshots are preserved even if the associated category is deleted. This ensures the audit trail remains intact for historical reference and compliance purposes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Implement GET operation to retrieve a single category snapshot by UUID identifier.

**Authorization:**
- Verify requester has admin role (regular or super administrator)
- Return 403 Forbidden if user is not an administrator
- No ownership check needed (all admins can view all category snapshots)

**Database Query:**
- Query ecommerce_mall_category_snapshots table by id (primary key)
- Include JOIN with ecommerce_mall_categories to validate category exists
- Include JOIN with ecommerce_mall_admins to retrieve administrator details
- Return 404 Not Found if snapshot does not exist

**Response Construction:**
- Map snapshot fields to IEcommerceMallCategorySnapshot DTO
- Include complete snapshot data: id, category_id, admin_id, previous_values, current_values, created_at, updated_at
- Parse previous_values and current_values as JSON objects in the response
- Include administrator information (email, grade) from joined admin record

**Error Handling:**
- 401 Unauthorized: User not authenticated
- 403 Forbidden: User is not an administrator
- 404 Not Found: Snapshot with given ID does not exist

**Performance Considerations:**
- Use indexed lookup on id (primary key)
- No pagination needed for single resource retrieval
- Cache snapshot data if frequently accessed for audit purposes

operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query ecommerce_mall_orders table with authorization filtering. For customer actor: add WHERE ecommerce_mall_customer_id = authenticatedCustomerId clause. For admin actor: no customer filter, returns all orders. Apply search filters from request body: status (enum filter), orderNumber (partial match), date range (created_at between startDate and endDate). Implement cursor-based pagination using created_at and id as cursor keys. Join with ecommerce_mall_order_items for item count if requested. Return summary fields only (id, orderNumber, status, totalPrice, createdAt, itemCount). Sort by created_at DESC, id DESC for consistent ordering. Validate status values against allowed enum. Handle empty result sets gracefully.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of shopping orders for the authenticated customer or all orders for administrators.

This operation provides comprehensive order history viewing capabilities with advanced filtering options. Customers can view their own orders with filters for order status, date ranges, and order number search. Administrators can view all platform orders with the same filtering capabilities for oversight and dispute resolution.

The response includes order summaries optimized for list displays, containing essential information such as order number, current status, total price, and creation timestamp. For detailed order information including all items and shipping address, use the GET /orders/{orderId} endpoint.

Pagination is implemented using cursor-based navigation for efficient large dataset handling. The response includes pagination metadata with cursors for navigating to previous and next pages.

Order status is derived from individual order item statuses and can be: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, or partiallyCompleted. Status filtering allows customers to quickly find orders in specific lifecycle stages.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for order list retrieval

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order summaries with navigation cursors

operations.description:
Retrieve complete details of a specific order including all purchased items, embedded shipping address snapshot, and associated shipments.

This operation provides comprehensive order information for customers to review their purchase details, track shipments, and verify order contents. Administrators can also access this endpoint for platform oversight and dispute resolution purposes.

The response includes the order's unique order number, creation timestamp, total price, and overall status derived from individual order item statuses. The shipping address is captured as a snapshot at the time of order placement and remains immutable even if the customer later modifies their saved addresses.

Each order item displays the purchased product variant, quantity, unit price at time of purchase, and current status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded). Items from different sellers are grouped by their respective shipments, each with tracking information and delivery status.

For orders containing multiple items, the overall order status is derived from the individual item statuses. An order is considered 'paid' when all items are paid, 'shipped' when all items are shipped, 'delivered' when all items are delivered, and 'partiallyCompleted' when items have mixed statuses.

Related operations include `PATCH /orders` for retrieving paginated order history and `GET /orders/{orderId}/items` for retrieving order items separately.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_orders table by orderId (UUID primary key). Verify authorization: customer must own the order (ecommerce_mall_customer_id matches authenticated customer) OR user must be admin. Include soft-deleted orders only for admin access.

Join with ecommerce_mall_order_items table to retrieve all order items for this order. For each order item, join with ecommerce_mall_product_variants to get variant details including SKU code and option values, and join with ecommerce_mall_products to get product name and main image.

Join with ecommerce_mall_shipments table to retrieve all shipments associated with this order. For each shipment, include tracking number, carrier name, shipped timestamp, and optional delivered timestamp. Map order items to their respective shipments.

Calculate average product ratings by querying ecommerce_mall_reviews for each product in the order items. Return null if no reviews exist.

Apply optimistic locking if concurrent modifications are possible. Return 404 if order not found or user lacks authorization. Return 403 if customer tries to access another customer's order.

responseBody.description: Complete order information with items and shipments

prerequisites.description: Order must be created before it can be retrieved by orderId

operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query ecommerce_mall_order_items table filtering by ecommerce_mall_order_id. Apply pagination with cursor-based navigation. Support filtering by status field (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded). Sort by created_at descending (newest first). Join with ecommerce_mall_products and ecommerce_mall_product_variants to include product name and variant options in response. Enforce ownership validation: customers can only access their own orders, administrators can access all orders. Return summary-level data optimized for list display including id, quantity, unit_price, status, product name, variant options, and created_at.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of order items belonging to a specific order.

This operation provides access to all purchased product variants within an order, including their quantities, unit prices at time of purchase, current status, and associated product information. Each order item represents an independent purchase with its own status lifecycle that can be cancelled or refunded separately from other items in the same order.

Customers can view their own order items to track purchase details and current status. Administrators have oversight access to view any order's items for dispute resolution and policy enforcement. The response includes product names and variant option values to provide complete context without requiring additional API calls.

Supports filtering by order item status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) and pagination with configurable page sizes. Results are sorted by creation date descending (newest items first). The unit price is immutable and reflects the price at time of purchase, preserved in order item snapshots for audit purposes.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering order items

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item summaries with product and variant information

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific order item within an order.

This operation returns the complete details of a purchased product variant within a customer's order, including quantity, unit price at time of purchase, current status, and product variant reference. The order item represents an individual purchased item that can have independent status tracking for cancellation and refund workflows.

**Access Control:**

- **Customers**: Can only access order items belonging to their own orders
- **Sellers**: Can access order items for products they sell (across all orders)
- **Administrators**: Can access any order item for platform oversight and dispute resolution

**Order Item Status:**

The status field indicates the current lifecycle state of the order item:
- `paid`: Payment completed, awaiting shipment
- `shipped`: Seller has shipped the item
- `delivered`: Customer has received the item
- `cancelled`: Item was cancelled (by customer, seller, or administrator)
- `refunded`: Item was refunded after delivery

**Related Operations:**

- `GET /orders/{orderId}`: Retrieve the parent order details
- `PATCH /orders/{orderId}/items`: List all items within an order
- `POST /order-items/{itemId}/cancellation-requests`: Request cancellation for eligible items
- `POST /order-items/{itemId}/refund-requests`: Request refund for delivered items
- `GET /order-item-snapshots`: View historical snapshots of this order item

**Data Preservation:**

The unit price is immutable after order creation and represents the price at time of purchase. This value is preserved in order item snapshots for dispute resolution and audit purposes. The product variant reference allows retrieval of current product information, though the snapshot preserves the variant state at purchase time.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_order_items table by id and verify ownership/authorization.

1. Validate both orderId and itemId are valid UUIDs
2. Query order_items table WHERE id = itemId AND ecommerce_mall_order_id = orderId
3. If no record found, return 404 Not Found
4. Verify authorization:
   - Get the order's ecommerce_mall_customer_id
   - If user is customer: verify user.id == order.ecommerce_mall_customer_id
   - If user is seller: verify product_variant.ecommerce_mall_product_id belongs to seller
   - If user is admin: allow access
5. If unauthorized, return 403 Forbidden
6. Return the order item with all fields: id, ecommerce_mall_order_id, ecommerce_mall_product_variant_id, quantity, unit_price, status, created_at, updated_at

parameters.description: Target order item's unique identifier (UUID format)
parameters.name: itemId

responseBody.description: Detailed order item information including quantity, unit price, status, and variant reference

prerequisites.description: Order must be created before order items can exist within it. Order items are created as part of the order creation process from shopping cart items.

operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query ecommerce_mall_order_item_snapshots table filtered by order_item_id. Implement data isolation based on user role: customers can only view snapshots for order items they purchased, sellers can view snapshots for order items containing their products, administrators can view all snapshots. Apply pagination with default page size 20, max 100. Sort by created_at descending (newest first) - this sort order is fixed and not user-configurable per section 855. Return pagination metadata with total count, current page, and total pages. Each snapshot summary includes snapshot_type, created_at, changed_by information, and preview of previous/current values. Validate that the order item exists before querying snapshots. Join with ecommerce_mall_admins table if changed_by_id is present to retrieve administrator information.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of audit trail snapshots for a specific order item.

This operation provides access to the complete history of changes made to an order item throughout its lifecycle, including initial purchase, status transitions, cancellation requests, and refund requests. Each snapshot captures the complete state of the order item at the time of the change, preserving product details (name, description), variant information (SKU, option values), pricing, and seller profile information as they existed at that moment.

Snapshots are critical for dispute resolution, purchase history verification, and maintaining a permanent record of all transactions on this money-exchange platform. The snapshots include: initial purchase snapshots capturing product and seller details at order placement, status change snapshots recording item status transitions, cancellation request snapshots documenting cancellation workflow, and refund request snapshots tracking refund processing.

Access control varies by user role: customers can view snapshots only for order items they purchased, sellers can view snapshots for order items containing their products, and administrators have unrestricted access to view all snapshots regardless of ownership. The snapshots are immutable and cannot be modified or deleted through any operation.

Results are sorted by creation timestamp in descending order (newest first), with this sort order being fixed and not user-configurable. Pagination uses a default page size of 20 snapshots per page with a maximum of 100 snapshots per page. The response includes comprehensive pagination metadata with total snapshot count, current page number, and total page count.

Related operations include retrieving order item details (GET /orders/{orderId}/items/{itemId}) and viewing order history (PATCH /orders).

requestBody.description: Pagination parameters and optional filters for snapshot query

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item snapshot summaries with metadata
